data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The answer is a non-concentration phenomenon (SRC_016's frame, pushed to a sharper law): the consensus probability does not converge to any single limit but the annealed probability tends to a constant c* \u2248 0.9, while the quenched (per-graph) probability is asymptotically a non-degenerate random variable on [0,1] \u2014 specifically e^{-X} where X is the basin-weighted Poisson count of stable-cycle obstructions of the drawn graph. Consensus probability averaged over graphs tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1; the obstruction structures are induced stable cycles (every vertex 2-same-colored via the cycle, third edge crossing) and paired-edge cuts; prevalence law: X converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean \u03bb = \u03a3_g \u03bb_g where \u03bb_g is the (computable) expected count of g-cycles whose third-edge structure admits a stable coloring, so P(quenched consensus) = e^{-X}, and P(annealed consensus) \u2192 E[e^{-X}] = exp(\u03bb(e^{-w} - 1)/w) for basin weights w.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Proof that the consensus indicator self-averages (annealed = quenched), which collapses this to a single constant and refutes the non-concentration claim","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Demonstration that basin-weighted intensities sum to 0 (then c* = 1) or diverge (then c* = 0)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Simulation showing finite-n consensus probabilities concentrating sharply across graph draws","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Random 3-regular graphs have Poisson-distributed short-cycle counts (configuration model: cycle of length g appears with mean (2^{g-1}/g)(1+o(1)) \u2014 famously (n-1).../2g giving constant means for fixed g). Each short induced cycle supports a canonical stable mixed coloring; longer cycles fail because a random 3-regular graph's induced cycles of length \u2265 C log n have third edges landing inside the cycle's own closure with non-vanishing probability, breaking stability. So the family of static attractors is Poisson(\u03bb) with \u03bb = O(1). The novel step: majority descent is LOCAL (radius-1), so whether a given cycle obstruction actually traps a run depends only on an O(cycle-length)-sized boundary process that is asymptotically independent across well-separated cycles; hence the trapping events form a thinned Poisson process with intensity \u03bbw, w a per-cycle basin weight. Quenched consensus probability = e^{-X} with X ~ Poisson(\u03bbw) depending on the drawn graph's cycle multiset \u2014 a genuinely random limit, matching the known non-self-averaging of cycle counts in random regular graphs. Annealed limit = E[e^{-X}] \u2208 (0,1).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
